caveats:
This product contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2026), processed by ESA and analyzed by the Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS).

This map was derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images acquired by the ALOS-2 and ALOS-4 satellites operated by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) using a pre-event time series (24 Apr 2026 and 22 May 2026) and a post-event acquisition (11 June 2026).

ALOS-2 and ALOS-4 data were provided by JAXA and analyzed by the Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS).

These are preliminary maps derived from satellite radar and should be used as guidance only. Coloured pixels may include false positives, and their absence does not mean an absence of damage or flooding.
methodology_other: Change detection on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images acquired before and after the event. Damage Proxy Maps show significant changes in radar coherence and amplitude; Flood Proxy Maps show areas that changed to standing water. Maps are preliminary and checked against news reports and ground-level imagery where available.

# Philippines Earthquake Mindanao: Damage Proxy Maps, Jun 2026

The **Earth Observatory of Singapore – Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS)** produced these damage proxy maps for Philippines Earthquake Mindanao (Jun 2026) from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images. Each map is a separate ZIP below with its GeoTIFF, a KMZ for Google Earth, the PNG figures and a text file describing how it was made and how to read it.

## Maps in this dataset

- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Mindanao, Philippines, Earthquakes, 16 June 2026, v0.9**
- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Mindanao, Philippines, Earthquakes, 13 June 2026, v0.5**
- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: West Mindanao, Philippines, Earthquakes, 09 June 2026, v0.8**

**More map details and files:** <https://sf.earthobservatory.sg/event/EOSRS_2026_003_PHL_EQ_202606_Mindanao>

**Legal Disclaimer:** <https://products.earthobservatory.sg/#/faq/>

**Credits:** Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS), Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2026)

organization.description: The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) is a research lab at Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore. It uses satellite remote sensing, mainly synthetic aperture radar (SAR), to map natural hazards and disasters. The lab produces Damage Proxy Maps (DPMs) and Flood Proxy Maps (FPMs) showing where damage or flooding has likely occurred. Its work focuses on Southeast Asia and the wider Asia-Pacific, and it also responds to major disasters worldwide.

EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Mindanao, Philippines, Earthquakes, 16 June 2026, v0.9

ZIP containing: GeoTIFF, KMZ, PNG, TXT.

The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) created this preliminary Damage Proxy Map (DPM) depicting areas that are likely damaged in Mindanao, Philippines, due to the Mw7.8 earthquake on 08 June 2026 and its aftershocks. This map was derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images acquired by the Copernicus Sentinel-1 satellite using a pre-event time series of (15 Feb 2026 to 03 June 2026) and a post-event acquisition (15 June 2026).
